scope: Atomic installation of package-qualified aliases and redefinitions over real compiler-generated B functions and mutable lexical closures.
implementation: An isolated owner installer validates a complete expected binding set, generation/hash-linked boot and runtime manifests, distinct unreserved code slots, exact public/internal export indices and body extents, function/pool metadata identity and arity before publication. The unchanged accepted lazy loader authenticates bytes/imports and installs both entries. A journal restores code rows, tables and cells on any failed transaction. Fresh code slots and retained instances keep old function objects callable.
oracle: Native CCL compiles two byte-identical target functions and a mutable closure factory, binds real case-sensitive symbols in two packages, and supplies behavior before and after rebinding. Native function-args/key vectors provide signatures. Generated calls dispatch through actual symbol cells and saved function objects, below and above 2 GiB. Python independently decodes exported body extents and joins every successful installation to binary digests and manifest history.
exclusions: Single Worker, synchronous trusted-owner transaction with Lisp execution and collection excluded. The byte provider must not re-enter installation or mutate owner memory. This is catalog integrity, not code signing or cross-Worker atomic publication.

The owner supplies existing D1 symbols, keyword identities, independently expected bindings, catalog and materialized function/pool objects. This is not a package allocator or the LL14 production cross-loader. Top-level metadata words must already equal pool elements zero and one; absent words refuse rather than being repaired.

Only the accepted non-retrying shared B profile is admitted here. The allocator-retry profile, bootstrap image ownership, generic-function method changes and code retirement are separate obligations. Old code is deliberately retained indefinitely; no unload or slot reuse policy is claimed.

Catalog metadata is trusted. Validation checks counts, keyword identities, record shapes and captures, not all nested debug contents. Keyword names are the admitted keyword-symbol subset; capture indices follow environment-slot order.

Entry ranges are complete binary function-body extents, including local declarations, joined to engine-validated export indices. They are not native machine-code addresses or inferred instruction entrypoints.

The compiler and integrated runtime are unchanged from accepted LL12. Native R6/R6a is reused by exact hashes while every native signature/behavior oracle and generated module is recompiled. The new installer remains an isolated proposal pending review and acceptance. No timing claim is made.
